BlackRock slashes IBIT in-kind conversion minimum to $1M –
Link
BlackRock cut the minimum for in-kind BTC-to-IBIT share conversions by 96%, from $25M to $1M. Cumulative in-kind conversions have topped $5B, up from $3B in October.
Matters because: Lower access barriers may move more wealth from self-custody into regulated ETF wrappers and deepen ETF-linked liquidity over time.

US Treasury sanctions Iran's digital asset industry for the first time –
Link
The US Treasury/OFAC expanded its "Economic Outcast" sanctions program to explicitly cover Iran's digital asset industry. The action targets exchanges, OTC desks, payment processors, and wallet addresses tied to IRGC-linked actors as the Iranian rial hit a historic low near 202,000 IRR/USD.
Matters because: It raises compliance risk for any exchange or infrastructure provider with exposure to Iran-linked flows and shows crypto rails are now a formal sanctions battleground.
